newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS HANDED EASY START IN OPEN DRAW.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS HANDED EASY START IN OPEN DRAW.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras and two of his fiercest tennis rivals were handed the easiest possible start in the Australian Open in the tournament draw made on Friday.
Sampras will play a qualifier in the first round at the National Tennis Centre in the first Grand Slam of the year, starting on Monday.
It is a fortune shared by second seed Michael Chang and fifth seed Thomas Muster, who were also pitted against players ranked well outside the world's top 100.

The draw, made by computer for the first time in Grand Slam history, allowed for a possible final between Sampras and defending champion Boris Becker, seeded sixth, in what would be a highly anticipated outcome given their recent rivalry.

In the women's singles, world number one Steffi Graf and Swiss teenager Martina Hingis were also drawn in opposite halves of the draw, allowing for a possible final encounter in a further potential boost for tournament organisers.

Sampras faces a tougher path to the final than Becker or world number two Chang, with Muster, third seed Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia and American Jim Courier, seeded 11, all barring the way for the top seed.
Becker, who ended a barren five-year period by winning in Melbourne last year, the German veteran's sixth Grand Slam title, will play unseeded Spaniard Carlos Moya in the first round.
Compatriot Graf, unbeatable in her last six Grand Slam tournaments and seeking her fifth Australian Open title, will play unseeded qualifier Janette Husarova of Slovakia in her first match.
Second seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain plays Italian Gloria Pizzichini, while fourth seed Hingis drew experienced German Barbara Rittner.

Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov, seeded four, would also have enjoyed a gentle introduction against a qualifier before he was forced to withdraw from the Open with a broken hand on Friday. His place in the draw was taken by American MaliVai Washington.
Of the original top five men's seeds, only Croatia's Goran Ivanisevic, chasing his first grand slam win, drew a non-qualifier.
He will face lowly-ranked wildcard Ben Ellwood of Australia.
Unseeded former women's champion Mary Pierce, whose victory in 1995 was the highlight of a career that has since declined, will face Russian Elena Likhovtseva, seeded 13, in a repeat of last year.
As defending champion, Pierce lost to Likhovtseva, then unseeded, in the second round in 1996, prompting coach Nick Bollettieri to sever their relationship after questioning her professionalism.

Unseeded Australian Mark Philippoussis, regarded as a dangerous floater in the draw after his shock third round defeat of Sampras last year, has been paired with fellow non-seed Tim Henman of Britain.
